clue.text: Gather Mark put back into job

blocks.note: to reap is to gather a harvest
a point is a mark, as in a decimal point

explanation.surface: Someone collects a man called Mark who has been restored to his old post.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name; it is just a dot or sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappoint someone is to name them again to a position they held before.

clue.text: Bucolic painting male replaced with rhino's head

indicators.note: replaced with means one letter is swapped out for another
'head' keeps only the first letter of 'rhino'

blocks.note: a mural is a wall painting
standard abbreviation; this is the letter taken out
first letter of rhino, the letter put in

explanation.surface: A country scene of a male figure is swapped for a rhinoceros head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic describes country life and the countryside, the same as rural; adjective synonym.

clue.text: Song about endless territory in battleground state

indicators.note: endless means losing the end, so a final letter is cut
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: an aria is a song in an opera
a zone is an area or territory

explanation.surface: A tune about land without limits in a fiercely contested region.
explanation.walkthrough: A battleground state is a US swing state that either party could win.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a US state that has been closely contested in recent presidential elections.

clue.text: Crew of old ship engaged in exercise

indicators.note: engaged in means involved inside something, so this piece sits within another

explanation.surface: The sailors of an ancient vessel are doing a training drill.
explanation.walkthrough: Crew suggests sailors, matching the ship; it is a gang of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group or gang of people, informally a crew of friends or followers.

clue.text: Really popular bible book bolstering theist's conclusion

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its final letter
in a down clue bolstering means propping up from below, so this piece comes underneath

blocks.note: the Book of Ruth in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A well-loved book of scripture supports the final position of a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: In truth is an adverbial phrase meaning really or actually.

clue.text: Ace abandons struggling Boston team? It's a grave sign!

indicators.note: abandons means leaves, so this letter is dropped from what follows
struggling suggests disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: A for ace, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: A star player quits a Boston sports side in trouble, which is a bad omen.
explanation.walkthrough: Grave sign reads as a serious omen; it is a marker over a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombstone is the inscribed stone marking a burial place, literally a sign on a grave.

clue.text: Fairground attraction regularly exhibited reindeer

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is shown

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A funfair shows off reindeer on a regular basis as its star turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride, such as a carousel or big wheel, is a typical attraction at a funfair.

clue.text: Composer from Berlin is sorely upset

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of a run of words
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

blocks.note: a run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A composer from the German capital is deeply distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin suggests a German composer, or Irving Berlin himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville and William Tell.

clue.text: Daughter read Poe's moving letters for brigand

indicators.note: moving letters means shifting the characters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl reads Edgar Allan Poe's touching letters about an outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving letters looks like touching correspondence; letters here are alphabet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, much like a brigand or bandit.

clue.text: Works out limits of elegant plaything

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

blocks.note: an athlete who works out trains

explanation.surface: Someone figures out the bounds of a stylish toy.
explanation.walkthrough: Works out reads as solves; it is exercising at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A model railway sold as a set is a classic toy, a plaything for children and hobbyists.

clue.text: Ill-treat young lady touring university quarter

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so one piece goes all the way around another

blocks.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
east is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A girl is mistreated while showing visitors around a part of a college town.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarter suggests a district of the university; in crosswords it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To misuse something or someone is to treat them badly or wrongly; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fellow follows heart in fall recess

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters are kept
follows says this piece comes after the other one in the answer

blocks.note: cove is old British slang for a man or chap

explanation.surface: A man is pursuing his heart during an autumn break.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall and recess sound like seasons and holidays; recess is a nook in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess set back into the wall of a room.

clue.text: Delusion about being immaculate

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone holds a false belief about being without sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Immaculate hints at religious purity, but here it just means spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsoiled has not been made dirty, so it is spotless and clean.

clue.text: Rushes back across north shore

indicators.note: back tells us to read this word from its end to its start
lying across something means stretched over it, so one piece is placed around another

explanation.surface: A person hurries back over the northern coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: Rushes could be the reeds by water; it is the verb for hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a poetic or literary word for a beach or shoreline.

clue.text: Consequently, those people are in favour of being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the words are listened to, so their sound counts

blocks.note: they're is those people are; for is in favour

explanation.surface: As a result, the crowd backs a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore means consequently or as a result; adverb synonym.

clue.text: Bird raised in hollow is cleaner

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: an egret is a heron-like bird

explanation.surface: A bird reared in a hole is cleaner than others.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleaner reads as a comparative adjective; it is a noun, a cleaning agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning substance used for washing clothes or dishes.

clue.text: Rowdy husband demolishing an igloo

indicators.note: demolishing knocks something apart, so its letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An unruly husband knocks down an igloo.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowdy looks like an adjective describing the husband but is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy is a noisy, rough person, which is what a hooligan is; noun synonym.

clue.text: Surgeon admitting death leads to terribly acrimonious feud

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside another
the leads of words are their first letters, taken from the following pair

blocks.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A surgeon confessing a fatality sparks a bitter, lasting quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long, bitter feud, originally a blood feud between families.

clue.text: Professional study on temperature is supported by model

indicators.note: in a down clue being supported means standing on top, so the next piece goes below

blocks.note: a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: An expert research project on heat is backed by an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Henry Ford's famous early car.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist is a member of a profession, a qualified practitioner; Professional is a broad noun definition.

clue.text: Consumed by fury, discontented vigilante becomes agent of retribution

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so this piece goes within the other
discontented means with its contents emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Eaten up by rage, an unhappy vigilante turns into an avenging figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger is someone who exacts revenge, a bringer of retribution.

clue.text: Extremely envious about line in legal arrangement

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is very jealous over a sentence in a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: C stands for circa, Latin for about, as in dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Escrow is a legal arrangement where a third party holds money or deeds until conditions are met.

clue.text: Arm mangled in brace

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A limb has been crushed and held in a support.
explanation.walkthrough: Arm suggests a limb in a brace; it means a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbine is a short rifle, a firearm, and arms are weapons.

clue.text: Ewe turns out to be alternative source of milk

indicators.note: turns out suggests something transformed, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A sheep proves to be a substitute supplier of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: Turns looks like part of the fodder's verb; it is part of the letters, with out as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet nurse breastfeeds another woman's baby, so she is a substitute provider of milk.

clue.text: Pen Charlie essentially twirled in exam

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so its central letter is taken
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: C is Charlie in the phonetic alphabet
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A pen belonging to Charlie spun around during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen looks like a writing tool, which suits the exam; it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is a pen or enclosure for horses or cattle.

clue.text: Criminal leads government a merry dance

indicators.note: leads means goes in front, so this piece comes first

explanation.surface: A crook leads the authorities a merry dance, giving them a runaround.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading someone a merry dance is an idiom for causing them trouble, which hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a lively dance done in a single line, a festive and merry one.

clue.text: White layer beneath exposed mass

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed
in a down clue beneath means placed underneath, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: a hen lays eggs, so is a layer

explanation.surface: A pale coat sits under a bulk that has been uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: Layer looks like a coat or stratum; it is something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale or grey-white, the colour of ash, as of a frightened face.

clue.text: Submissive female catches chill, periodically

indicators.note: catching something holds it, so one piece is held inside another
periodically means at intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a doe is a female deer

explanation.surface: A meek woman catches a cold now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Docile means meek and easily managed, ready to obey; adjective synonym.

clue.text: German ill-equipped to comprehend Ghana's armed struggle

indicators.note: to comprehend is literally to take in, so one piece goes inside another

explanation.surface: A German is not prepared to understand Ghana's military conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunfight is a fight with firearms, a literal armed struggle.

clue.text: They say it was wild in Marlowe's time

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: People claim life was untamed in the days of the playwright Marlowe.
explanation.walkthrough: They say looks like a sound signal and Marlowe's time like a period; the definition is the whole of the first part, from the phrase Wild West.
explanation.definitionFit: The American frontier is popularly called the Wild West, so people say that region was wild.

clue.text: Infernal substance 17 removes with electronic article

blocks.note: 17 is the dentist, who scrapes off this hard deposit from teeth

explanation.surface: A hellish material is removed, along with an online piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to the answer to 17 down; Tartarus was the hell of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartarean means belonging to Tartarus, the underworld of Greek myth, so hellish or infernal.
